caseno: Criminal Petition for Special Leave to Appeal No. 26 of 1989.
lawyer:
Mr. Mainul Hosein, Advocate, (Mr. Md. Joynul Abedin, Advocate with him) instructed by Mr. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Petitioner.
Mr. B. Hossain, Deputy Attorney-General instructed by Mr. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Respondent.
parties:
Shah Alam Chowdhury -------------- Petitioner
Vs. 
The State ----------------- Respondent.
full_judgment:
2. T e impugned judgment runs into about 40 pages and the main grievance made by the learned advocate for the petitioner before us is that much of the judgment was unnecessary while some parts thereof including findings with regard to the pending proceeding are prejudicial to the accused in the matter of their defence. In order to appreciate the said grievance it is necessary to state the facts of the case briefly as they appear in the judgment. 

 3. The case involves the alleged murder of one Nuru Miah Chowdury. The wife of the deceased lodged an FIR on 2.11.86 at Dhanmondi P. S. giving rise to Dhanmondi P. S. Case No. 3(11) 86. On 9.11.86 the present petitioner was arrested in connection with this case. As the investigation could not be completed within the time-frame under section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Magistrate passed an order on 30.8.87 under sub-section (5) of the said section stopping further investigation and releasing the accused person. The case was, however, revived under sub-section (7 A) by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka by order dated 6.9.87. The CID however, submitted a final report on 6.10.87 and the accused were discharged by an order of the even date. Thereafter on 14.7.88 the Senior Assistant Superintendent of Police, CID, Dhaka submitted a petition before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate praying for orders for further investigation of the case which was allowed and ultimately charge sheet was submitted on 25.8.88 against the petitioner and others. The Sessions Judge, Dhaka received the case record on 1.12.88 and took cognizance under sections 302/201, 364/34 Penal Code. The petitioner made a prayer for bail which was rejected by the Sessions Judge for the second time on 8.2.89. On that date charges were framed against the accused including one under sections 302/34 Penal Code. The petitioner then moved the High Court Division for bail and a rule was issued on 13.2.89 (Criminal Misc. Case No. 46/89). A Suo Motu rule No. 47/89 was also issued on the day calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and others to show cause why the order dated 14.7.88 passed by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka permitting further investigation into the case should not be set aside and why the Government should not be directed to consider whether it should revive the case under sub-section (7A) of section 167 Cr. P. C. 

 4. After lengthy consideration of all conceivable matters it was found that there was a prima facie case against the petitioner under sections 302/34 Penal Code and as such he was not entitled to bail. 

 5. As to the suo motu rule it was found upon a consideration of all aspects of the law that the Police validly made further investigation under section 173 (3B) Cr. P. C. with the approval of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka from 14.7.88 and validly submitted the charge sheet. Thus there was no occasion to advert to the second part of the suo motu rule asking the Government to consider the question of revival of the case. In the result both the rules were discharged. 

 6. Mr. Mainul Hosein, learned Advocate for the petitioner, as already noticed, has not much to say about the rejection of the prayer for bail but he has referred to certain observations in the judgment, for example, "as dictated by petitioner Shah Alam Chowdhury, the alleged principal architect and perpetrator of murder of the deceased," which according to him will greatly prejudice the accused at the trial. The petitioner need have no such apprehension but even then it may be observed that the guilt or otherwise of the accused will be determined only upon the evidence to be adduced in the case and not with reference to anything else. 

 7. As to the other finding in the suo motu rule that the charge-sheet was validly submitted, Mr. Mainul Hosein has argued that the said finding has debarred the accused from raising the question at the trial that the revival of the case and submission of the charge-sheet upon such revival was contrary to the provision under section 167 Cr. P.C. We do not find much force in the contention of Mr. Hosein, firstly, because, as has been noticed above, the charge-sheet was submitted not upon revival of the case under section 167 but following further investigation under section 173 Cr.P.C. The High Court Division is right in holding that the power to make a further investigation is available to the Police if there has been no order under section 167 stopping the proceeding and releasing the accused after the expiry of the period of investigation under the said section. Secondly the petitioner does not seem to have raised the question at any stage that the submission of the charge-sheet was bad in law. Charges having already been framed and the trial having begun for making a prayer for discharging the accused on that ground has already gone by. In the High Court Division also no such plea seems to have been raised. In deed we have failed to understand what prompted the learned Judges to issue the suo motu rule when nobody was making a grievance against submission of b the charge sheet or the proceeding. The exercise undertaken by the learned Judges was no doubt a pains taking and scholarly one by firstly raising a hypothetical proposition suo motu and then successfully demolishing it, but it must be said, with respect, that there was a profound absence of any necessity or purpose for the same. The petitioner will be entitled to take any defence as may be advised but subject to the finding of the High Court Division that the chargesheet has been validly submitted.
